headline: Lula wins a fourth term and Flávio Bolsonaro rejects the count, a US intelligence memo on Iranian plots empties Gulf embassies, and Cyclone Arnab heads for Andhra Pradesh
standfirst: The weekend strike on Iran that a US envoy floated did not happen by Sunday, but the blockade passed 100 days and Brent settled at 116.72 dollars. The Houthis fired three missile waves at Saudi Arabia, Israel votes on Tuesday under a West Bank closure, and France counted 1,314 arrests in Saturday's protests. In India, IMD expects Cyclone Arnab to cross the Andhra coast around 28 October, Kharge's remark in Patna has the BJP planning protests today, and Jamia has moved all classes online. On Hacker News, a root shell on a Samsung TV leads and Dan Luu's essay on ambitious software draws the most comments.
notes: First Phoenix run of 26 October. No browser tool was connected, so the owner's X feed was not read; one web search for what is trending in tech and AI on X stood in for it and found nothing newer than a 23 October market trend about AI investment doubts.

Ground News: the home page showed only the Daily Briefing card (8 stories, 1,168 articles, led by the DNI memo on Iranian plots, with teasers for the Alaska Senate certification fight, Brazil's runoff and a measles outbreak at 4,588 cases); its story list was cut off both times it was read. /interest/world returned an empty page again. /interest/india was read in full: Dhanush on Jailer 2 (23 sources), Jamia moves classes online (19), Jaishankar on West Asia and Ukraine (8), and the India-Russia trade Blindspot (now 13 sources, only 17% left).

Follow-up to yesterday: the 25 October edition led with a US envoy saying a strike on Iran could come this weekend. No strike had been reported by Sunday evening; analysts point to the 3 November US midterms as a brake.

Not carried: a roundup put the toll at Riyadh airport at 12 killed, but no primary report supports it (Al Jazeera reported two killed at King Fahd airport on 22 October). The school-assembly digest again lists Ashoke Sen as the first Indian to win the Oskar Klein Medal; this was still not confirmed by a second source. Forecast winds for Cyclone Arnab differ between outlets, so the card gives the range.
All ten tech pages sent for reading loaded. The Samsung TV root claim and the skin-cancer comparison rest on their authors' own write-ups and are flagged unverified.

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: The Hacker News front page and the tech press. The X feed was not reachable this run.

stories.title: Root shell on a Samsung TV tops Hacker News, with claims about always-on microphones and ad tracking
stories.summary: A researcher's post about rooting a Samsung TV leads HN with 794 points and 608 comments. Public write-ups show root on 2025 and 2026 Tizen sets through Developer Mode; the data-collection claims are not verified.
stories.heat: HN 794 pts (day's max), 608 comments · Tom's Hardware coverage · several GitHub write-ups · no Samsung statement found
detail: The HN link is a post on X by the account @log4j, who said on 21 October that a 2025 Samsung TV yielded a root shell and tied it to an always-on microphone, automatic content recognition and ad targeting. The post promised a write-up but did not include one. Tom's Hardware covered the claims; they remain unverified.

Separate public research does show root on these sets. A GitHub repository by Swarnaditya Singh describes rooting a 2026 Tizen 9.0 TV in Developer Mode: the SDB daemon on TCP port 26101 accepts an unquoted '0 appinstall tpk' command (cited as SVE-2025-50109), which gives a user-level shell, and a signed dotnet host then gives root. The author removed 84 preinstalled packages and says the result covers one model and one firmware.

Issues on a second project, chris-ritsen/samsung-tv-root, report root on a UE43DU7100 (tested 20 October) and boot-persistent root on an older Tizen 6.0 set (tested 24 October). No response or patch from Samsung turned up in searches.

stories.title: Dan Luu's 'We should be more ambitious with the software we build' climbs to 755 points and the day's most comments
stories.summary: Luu argues AI coding tools make once-infeasible projects practical, with a counterpoint from Yossi Kreinin. It was a 46 yesterday and is now the busiest thread on HN.
stories.heat: HN 755 pts, 697 comments (day's most) · up from yesterday's run · single-platform story
detail: Dan Luu cites projects that AI coding tools made practical: Michael Malis's pgrust, a Postgres rewrite that found real Postgres bugs, Luu's own regex engine, a faster ripgrep fork and a faster Rust build setup. He argues the gap between what models can implement and what they can verify has grown, so hard tasks still need human guidance.

An appendix carries Yossi Kreinin's counterpoint: most people should be less ambitious with AI-built software, because pass and fail criteria are weak and the resulting code is opaque. The thread has 697 comments, the most on the front page this morning.

stories.title: A ten-year-old CNN beats GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at skin-lesion diagnosis in a dermatologist's test
stories.summary: On 200 biopsy-confirmed lesions, a fine-tuned Inception v3 got 62% right against 42% for each frontier model. One author, one run per model.
stories.heat: HN 479 pts, 217 comments · author's own blog · no press pickup found
detail: Dr Magnus Lynch, a consultant dermatologist at Guy's Hospital and honorary reader at King's College London, posted on 25 October that he tested three systems on 200 histology-confirmed lesions from the public MILK10k dataset, with six possible diagnoses.

The fine-tuned Inception v3 CNN was right on 125 of 200 (62%), GPT-6 Astra on 84 (42%) and Claude Fable 5.1 on 85 (42%). For melanoma as first choice, the CNN found 13 of 30, Claude Fable 5.1 found 11 and GPT-6 Astra 8. Lynch notes the small sample, a single run per model and that the CNN is a deliberately modest baseline.

stories.title: iFixit gives the iPhone Duo a 5 out of 10, its best score yet for a foldable, as Apple's 2,000-dollar phone sells out in Beijing
stories.summary: The teardown finds two batteries totalling 19.1 Wh and a 999-dollar inner-screen repair. CNBC reports strong demand and scalpers at the Beijing launch.
stories.heat: HN 59 pts, 21 comments · iFixit · CNBC (two reports) · Google News coverage of an iPhone Duo 2 · broad, steady
detail: iFixit's teardown, dated 25 October, gives the iPhone Duo a provisional repairability score of 5 out of 10, the highest it has given a foldable. The inner display and hinge cost it the most: out-of-warranty inner-display damage is 999 dollars, and a cover-layer service is 49 dollars, or 19 with AppleCare. The two batteries (7.5 Wh and 11.6 Wh) use electrically debonding adhesive.

iFixit also notes hinge crunching from dust and a suspected stress point near the centre hinge linked to reported screen cracks. CNBC reports strong demand for the roughly 2,000-dollar phone and scalpers targeting buyers at the Beijing launch, and reports say Apple is already working on an iPhone Duo 2.

stories.title: Why OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices by up to 80%, and IBM's CEO says open-weight models are now 'irresistibly good and cheap'
stories.summary: Max Woolf traces the summer's price cuts to open-weight pressure. IBM's Arvind Krishna says open models deliver about 90% of frontier quality at 10 to 25% of the token cost.
stories.heat: HN 195 pts, 221 comments (Woolf) and 56 pts (The Register) · two independent sources
detail: Max Woolf's post of 25 October lists the cuts: GPT-5.6 Luna down 80% on 30 July, GPT-6.1 Sol cache reads halved on 29 September, and Claude Opus 5.5 at 4 dollars in and 20 out per million tokens. He points at open-weight models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (0.15 and 0.60 dollars, now on 29 OpenRouter providers against 13 in May) and asks whether the timing relates to rumoured OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs.

The Register reports that IBM CEO Arvind Krishna told the Q3 earnings call on 21 October that open-weight models now cost 10 to 25% of frontier models per token while being about 90% as effective, and that on-prem AI interest is booming. IBM's revenue was 17.1 billion dollars, up 5%.

stories.title: Doubts about AI spending hit tech stocks: Nasdaq's worst day since June, Meta down nearly 7%
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% on 23 October after Meta's AI capex pushed free cash flow negative. SK Hynix rose after scrapping the Solidigm IPO.
stories.heat: X trending topic (23 Oct) · CNBC (several reports) · peaked Friday, markets reopen today
detail: An X trending topic on 23 October reported the Nasdaq Composite down 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June, with Meta Platforms sliding nearly 7% despite beating estimates. CNBC tied Meta's fall to heavy AI spending pushing its free cash flow negative.
In the same week CNBC reported OpenAI nearing a funding round at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation led by UAE investors, and SK Hynix shares rising over 4% after it scrapped its planned Solidigm IPO.

stories.title: Eugene, Oregon quotes a local outlet 2.5 million dollars for records about one police officer
stories.summary: The Intercept reports the city estimated 44,816 staff hours for a misconduct records request. The outlet is appealing.
stories.heat: HN 427 pts, 115 comments · The Intercept (published 1 October, resurfaced today)
detail: Lauren Harper of the Freedom of the Press Foundation writes that the City of Eugene estimated at least 44,816 staff hours and about 2,484,599 dollars to answer Double Sided Media's request for records about officer Justin Peckels from 2018 to 2026. A second request about a former officer was quoted at 195,870 dollars, for a total near 2.7 million.
The outlet is appealing. The piece calls for fee caps, public-interest waivers for journalists and better search software.

stories.title: 'I refuse to accept a censored Internet': FOSDEM 27 opens a Digital Dissident devroom
stories.summary: The room wants talks on circumvention, metadata-resistant messaging and secure publishing, each with a threat model. Proposals close 30 November.
stories.heat: HN 420 pts, 207 comments · organiser's blog · single-platform story
detail: Bogomil Shopov, one of the devroom managers, posted on 25 October inviting proposals for the Digital Dissident devroom at FOSDEM 27, held at ULB Campus Solbosch in Brussels on 30 and 31 January 2027.
The call opened on 24 October and closes on 30 November at 23:59 UTC; speakers hear back on 2 December and the schedule is published on 7 December.

stories.title: DreamHost resets email and FTP passwords during an incident that has kept File Manager down since Thursday
stories.summary: The status page lists an active incident since 23 October affecting webmail and File Manager, with precautionary password resets for some users.
stories.heat: HN 130 pts, 55 comments · DreamHost status page · no press coverage found
detail: DreamHost's status page shows an incident that began on 23 October at 2:20 PM PDT, still marked Identified at 11:43 AM PDT on 25 October. File Manager is unavailable and Email, Webmail and phpMyAdmin are listed as affected.

The company reset passwords for some email and FTP or SFTP users as a precaution and is emailing steps to affected account owners. It warns that it never asks for a password by email or through a login link.

stories.title: Amazon's new kids' tablets for ages 3 and up draw a 'digital pacifier' critique
stories.summary: Oligarch Watch cites pediatric research linking screen-based calming to weaker executive function. Amazon disputes the framing.
stories.heat: HN 115 pts, 170 comments · single Substack source
detail: Caleb Ecarma's 21 October post criticises marketing for Amazon's 8.7-inch and 11-inch Android Kids Tablets, such as 'Enough for the flight', and quotes University of Michigan pediatrician Jenny Radesky. It cites a September 2026 JAMA Pediatrics umbrella review covering more than 2.8 million children.
The tablets include generative AI features and a free 12-month Kids+ subscription that renews at up to 8.99 dollars a month. An Amazon spokesperson disputed the description of the battery marketing.

stories.title: Also: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, the state of context engineering, F-Zero X on the 3DS, and Ukraine's Starlink alternative
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: HN 439 pts (Imagination Library), 100 pts (context engineering), 77 pts (F-Zero X), 56 pts (Next.js) · CNBC
detail: On HN: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which mails free books to children (439 points), Drew Breunig on the state of context engineering (100), a postmortem of porting F-Zero X to the Nintendo 3DS (77), and a blogger who reached 100 on every Lighthouse category by removing Next.js (56).
CNBC reports Ukraine is looking for a Starlink alternative with Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE while SpaceX keeps restricting Starlink service there.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.blurb: Ground News Daily Briefing (the World page was empty), Axios, Al Jazeera, NPR, CNN, CBS News, the Times of Israel, Votebeat and CNBC.

stories.title: US intelligence memo says Iranian plots against Americans are in 'advanced stages'; embassies across the Gulf cut staff
stories.summary: DNI Jay Clayton warned Rubio that Iran has 'substantially increased' efforts to target Americans. The expected weekend strike did not come, the blockade passed 100 days and Brent settled at 116.72 dollars.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing lead (8 stories, 1,168 articles) · Axios scoop, The Week, IBTimes, The American Conservative · Brent at its highest since April · escalating
detail: Axios obtained a one-page unclassified memo dated 23 October from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. It says Iran has 'substantially increased' efforts to target Americans and that lethal plots have reached 'advanced stages' in the Middle East and elsewhere. It names no targets or dates.

The State Department ordered family members and non-essential staff out of the embassy in Riyadh and the consulates in Jeddah and Dhahran on 21 October, and later cut staff in the UAE, Lebanon, Qatar and Jordan, according to a US official quoted in the reports. A State Department spokesperson was reported as saying the order covered Saudi Arabia only, so the scope is disputed.

The strike that US envoy Tom Barrack said could come 'as early as this weekend' had not been reported by Sunday evening; analysts cited by Forex.com point to the 3 November midterms as a brake. CENTCOM says the blockade of Iranian ports, now past 100 days, has kept at least 25 billion dollars of Iranian crude off the market.
Brent settled at 116.72 dollars ahead of Sunday's reopening, its highest since April, according to FinanceFeeds. Zerodha's market feed showed Brent near 115 dollars this morning.

stories.title: Lula wins a fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro 51.8% to 48.2%; Bolsonaro says he will not accept the result
stories.summary: With all votes counted, Lula led by nearly 4.4 million votes after trailing in the first round. Flávio Bolsonaro plans a legal challenge.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing teaser · NPR, CNN, CBS News, Rio Times · also on HN (12 pts) · fresh this morning
detail: Brazil's electoral court count gives Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva 51.8% against 48.2% for Flávio Bolsonaro in the 25 October runoff, a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes, according to CNN and NPR. It is Lula's fourth, non-consecutive term.
Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump ally, led the 4 October first round with 47.03% to Lula's 45.16%. He said he would not accept the result and would challenge it in court, CNN reports.

CBS News says the campaign turned on the cost of living, crime and corruption. Earlier partial counts showed a narrower split of about 51.5% to 48.5%, which is why some outlets give slightly different figures.

stories.title: Israel votes on Tuesday with the West Bank closed and a Hebron operation displacing over 2,600 people
stories.summary: Polls put Netanyahu's bloc at 49 to 55 seats, short of 61. Crossings from the West Bank stay shut until after the vote.
stories.heat: Times of Israel live blog, Haaretz live, CNN, AP via Washington Times, NPR · vote in two days
detail: CNN calls Tuesday's general election a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. Most polls give his bloc of Likud, two far-right and two ultra-Orthodox parties 49 to 55 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot used his final rally to warn that Netanyahu would do whatever it takes to stay in power.

The army is running a large operation centred on Hebron after a gun attack killed two Israeli soldiers. The Palestinian Authority says 2,670 people have been displaced, according to the Times of Israel. Haaretz reports a general closure on West Bank Palestinians for election day, a ban on Palestinian workers in settlements and closed land crossings until after the vote.

stories.title: Houthis fire three missile waves at Riyadh's airport and Saudi bases; the coalition says it shot down 12 missiles and two drones
stories.summary: Debris injured two people. Riyadh's King Khalid airport reopened two terminals, but most flights were cancelled.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera (two reports), PBS, AFP · Brent reaction · second straight day of escalation
detail: The Houthis said on 25 October that they fired dozens of ballistic missiles in three waves, at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, King Khalid air base in Khamis Mushait and a naval base in Jazan, as retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sanaa the day before, Al Jazeera reports.

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted 12 missiles and two drones. Saudi Civil Defence said debris from two missiles injured two people. Two terminals at King Khalid airport resumed operations, but Flightradar24 showed most flights cancelled. The Houthis also advanced on Jabal Sabr near Taiz. Neither side's figures are independently verified.

stories.title: France reports 1,314 arrests and 500 extra soldiers guard Milan as protests sweep European cities
stories.summary: Marches over the cost of living ran from Paris to Rome, Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana, with brief clashes in Rome and Turin.
stories.heat: NPR, PBS (AP), CBS News · second weekend running · counts differ by outlet
detail: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said police made 1,314 arrests in nationwide protests on Saturday over the cost of living and the education system, CBS News reports; yesterday's edition carried nearly 1,000 from an earlier count.

AP, carried by NPR and PBS, reports 500 soldiers sent to Milan on top of hundreds already there, with about 5,000 police. The Milan march stayed peaceful; there were brief clashes in Rome and Turin. Italian police reported nine arrests and 371 people briefly detained in eight cities.

stories.title: Democrats and voting-rights groups fight the Justice Department's suit to block Alaska's Senate result if Sullivan loses
stories.summary: Trump says he ordered the suit, which cites a second 'Dan Sullivan' on the ballot. Experts call it without precedent.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing teaser · Votebeat, CNBC, CNN, ABC, Bloomberg, Alaska Beacon · midterms on 3 November
detail: The Justice Department sued in federal court in Anchorage on 22 October, asking that the Senate result not be certified, and that it be investigated, if anyone other than Senator Dan Sullivan wins. It argues that a second candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan, will confuse voters; Alaska's supreme court had already ordered him onto the ballot.

'I'm the one that said do it,' Trump told reporters, according to ABC News. CNBC reports that Democratic candidate Mary Peltola and a voting-rights group have filed challenges arguing the federal executive has no authority over state-run elections.

stories.title: Russia agrees to US-brokered talks in November but rules out a ceasefire as strikes continue
stories.summary: Putin told Witkoff talks can resume in November, the first round since February. Recent Russian strikes cut power to more than 500,000 people.
stories.heat: CNBC, NBC News, CNN, Business Standard, Stratfor · latest reports 21 to 23 October · steady
detail: After meeting US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg, Putin said Moscow is ready to resume talks with Kyiv in November, CNBC reports. Zelensky hopes for early November. Stratfor's summary is that Moscow agreed to talks but ruled out a ceasefire.

Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves, and Ukraine's Energy Ministry said one attack cut power to more than 500,000 people. Russia said Ukraine sent 630 drones towards Moscow. No new major development was reported for 25 October.

stories.title: Also: a US measles outbreak at 4,588 cases, China's Fifth Plenum, Rubio on Pakistan, and Carney's defence deal with Turkey
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing teaser · Stratfor · CBC
detail: Ground News's briefing teases a measles outbreak that has reached 4,588 cases; the card did not give a country or source, so the figure is not checked here. Stratfor previews China's Fifth Plenum preparing the Communist Party for internal and external challenges.
Marco Rubio said the US must keep ties with Pakistan 'from a geographic standpoint', and CBC reports Mark Carney's defence-industry cooperation with Turkey is testing his geopolitical ambitions.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Ground News /interest/india, ANI, Deccan Herald, ThePrint, WION, Variety, Indian Opinion and national outlets. Single-source items are flagged unverified.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab to cross the Andhra coast around 28 October as a very severe storm; red alerts from Odisha to Kerala
stories.summary: IMD expects landfall between roughly Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. Odisha has shut schools in five southern districts for 28 and 29 October.
stories.heat: ANI, Deccan Herald, Gujarat Samachar, school-assembly digest · system named since yesterday · escalating
detail: The Bay of Bengal system flagged in yesterday's edition is now Cyclone Arnab. ANI reports IMD expects it to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the Andhra Pradesh coast around 28 October. One report gives a crossing zone between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, another a wider stretch from West Godavari to Srikakulam.

Forecast winds differ by outlet, from 115 to 125 km/h gusting to 140, up to a 120 to 165 km/h range. Red alerts cover Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli for 27 October and Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri in Odisha for 28 October, according to Deccan Herald and ANI.

Odisha has closed schools and colleges in those five districts for 28 and 29 October, cancelled leave for disaster staff and hoisted distant cautionary signal No. 1 at all ports. Fishermen are told not to go to sea until 29 October. Red alerts also cover Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Kerala.

stories.title: Kharge's 'Modi ka baap bhi jayega' in Patna: BJP calls it indecent and plans nationwide protests today
stories.summary: Amit Shah says Kharge 'tore apart all norms of decorum'. A police complaint has been filed and the BJP wants an apology from Rahul Gandhi.
stories.heat: ThePrint (PTI), Hans India, News Karnataka, Indian Opinion · protests set for Monday · rising
detail: Speaking in Patna on 25 October at an event for the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister, Shri Krishna Singh, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge answered a heckler who shouted that Modi would not go without a rebellion. His reply, 'Modi ka baap bhi jayega', was widely reported.

BJP president Nitin Nabin called it indecent and unparliamentary, Amit Shah said on X that Kharge had 'torn apart all norms of decorum', and Ravi Shankar Prasad called it shameful. A police complaint has been filed, ThePrint reports, and the BJP says it will protest nationwide today and burn an effigy of Kharge at Income Tax Circle in Patna. Congress's full reply was not found.

stories.title: Jamia Millia Islamia moves all classes online as the protest for a student union enters its second week
stories.summary: Students want JMISU elections restored after 20 years. Police detained four and the campus gates are closed.
stories.heat: Ground News /interest/india 19 sources (47% right) · WION, The Statesman, Free Press Journal, Daily Jagran · escalating
detail: A registrar's notice dated 24 October moved all courses online 'until further notice', citing student safety. The protest began on 12 October with a demand to restore elections to the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union, dissolved in 2006, and the removal of the chief proctor. Some students are on hunger strike.

Daily Jagran reports police detained four people, including student leaders, and the university closed its gates. The university says a committee is drafting the union's constitution; its account and the students' account of the confrontation differ.

stories.title: Jio Platforms lists on 28 October, with a grey-market premium of about 22%
stories.summary: The IPO closed 22 times subscribed last week. The premium figure comes from one aggregator.
stories.heat: Indian Opinion digest · follows yesterday's 70-score close · listing in two days
detail: Indian Opinion's daily digest says Jio Platforms' shares list on 28 October and quotes a grey-market premium of 22%. Yesterday's edition reported the issue closed about 22 times subscribed.
Grey-market premiums are unofficial and change daily; no second outlet confirming the figure was found this morning.

stories.title: Dhanush calls Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 a must-watch as the film passes its second weekend
stories.summary: Rajinikanth's former son-in-law reviewed the film; 23 outlets picked it up. Jailer 2 opened at No. 2 worldwide with 31.2 million dollars.
stories.heat: Ground News /interest/india 23 sources (52% right), the India page's top story · Variety, Koimoi
detail: Dhanush, who was married to Rajinikanth's daughter Aishwarya, praised Jailer 2 as a must-watch; it is the most-covered India story on Ground News this morning with 23 sources.

Variety reports the film opened on 15 October and was the second-biggest film worldwide over 16 to 18 October with 31.2 million dollars, behind Street Fighter. Its four-day India gross was an estimated 224 crore rupees, the third-highest four-day start for a Tamil film. Koimoi puts day-one worldwide at about 127 crore rupees.

stories.title: Markets brace for a weak Monday after four straight Sensex losses, with Brent near 115 dollars
stories.summary: The Sensex closed at 73,124 on 23 October, down 2.1% for the week. GIFT Nifty points lower this morning.
stories.heat: Trading Economics, Business Standard, Zerodha Pulse · oil tied to Gulf news
detail: Trading Economics reports the Sensex closed at 73,124 on 23 October, down 0.17% and its fourth straight loss, for a weekly fall of 2.1%. Business Standard reported the Nifty near 22,600, with mid and small caps falling sharply.
Zerodha's Pulse feed says GIFT Nifty pointed to a negative open on Monday 26 October, with Brent around 115 dollars after the weekend's Gulf news.

stories.title: Jaishankar: India 'cannot remain helpless spectators' to the wars in West Asia and Ukraine; at the UN, India calls Pakistan's military its 'real rulers'
stories.summary: The minister pressed for dialogue and diplomacy, and India's UN statement said terrorism as statecraft is unacceptable.
stories.heat: Ground News /interest/india 8 sources (88% right) · school-assembly digest
detail: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar pressed for 'dialogue and diplomacy' over the wars in West Asia and Ukraine, saying India cannot remain a helpless spectator; Ground News lists 8 sources.
At the UN, India said Pakistan's military remains the country's 'real rulers' and that using terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is unacceptable, according to the daily digest.

stories.title: Indian airlines' suspension of Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam flights leaves Kerala workers stranded
stories.summary: Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa paused services until at least 24 October. Riyadh airport has partly reopened, but whether the suspensions were extended is not confirmed.
stories.heat: Indian Opinion digest · Madhyamam · linked to the Houthi card
detail: Indian Opinion reports that Houthi attacks on Saudi airports have disrupted flights from Kerala since 8 October, and that Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa Air suspended Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam services until at least 24 October.
Madhyamam reports Riyadh's airport has partly reopened. No airline statement on whether the pause was extended past 24 October was found, so check with the airline before travel.

stories.title: RBI governor says upper-layer NBFCs must list, a hint at Tata Sons
stories.summary: Sanjay Malhotra's remark points at core investment companies. One aggregator source.
stories.heat: Indian Opinion digest only
detail: Indian Opinion reports RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said upper-layer non-bank finance companies, including core investment companies such as Tata Sons, will have to list. Tata Sons has long sought to avoid a listing.
No wire or business-paper report of the remark was found this morning.

stories.title: India and Russia aim for 100 billion dollars in trade by 2030, still a Ground News Blindspot
stories.summary: Second day on the India page, now at 13 sources with only 17% from the left.
stories.heat: Ground News /interest/india 13 sources (up from 12), Blindspot, only 17% left · Reuters-sourced
detail: Ground News still flags the Modi and Putin push for 100 billion dollars of bilateral trade by 2030 as a Blindspot: of 13 sources, only 17% lean left. It was carried yesterday at 12 sources.

stories.title: Also: Mann ki Baat on Vocal for Local, ISRO's four launch pads by 2029, a narco-cartel bust in the Northeast, and Pollard to coach Mumbai Indians
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: Daily Jagran digest · Indian Opinion
detail: PM Modi's Mann ki Baat asked listeners to back 'Vocal for Local' before Deepavali. ISRO chairman Narayanan said India will have four launch pads by 2029. Amit Shah called an operation in Assam, Mizoram and Manipur a 'lethal blow' to an international narco-cartel.

Karnataka's D.K. Shivakumar warned IT firms against sidelining Kannadigas in hiring, and Congress has asked the SP for 170 seats in Uttar Pradesh for 2027. In sport, India won its first mixed doubles medal at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in 72 years, and Kieron Pollard was named head coach of Mumbai Indians.
